stemBlocks.value: On the grid, O is the origin, P is the point (−2, 4) and R is the point (5, 1). (iii) Write the position vector OR as a column vector. (iv) Q is such that QR = (2, −4); plot Q. (v) Determine |QR|. (vi) Show by calculation that OPQR is a parallelogram.
Think first: Read the coordinates straight off the grid, then remember that QR runs from Q to R — so to find Q you go backwards from R.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p285-q08 from workbook page 285.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the coordinates of R from the grid and write them as a column vector.

contentBlocks.value: R is 5 units right and 1 unit up from O

solutionSteps.instruction: Since QR = OR − OQ, rearrange to OQ = OR − QR and substitute.

contentBlocks.value: Result: Q = (3, 5); plot the point 3 right and 5 up

solutionSteps.instruction: Apply Pythagoras to the components of QR.
Write the vectors of one pair of opposite sides of OPQR.
State the conclusion. Equal vectors mean the sides are both parallel and of equal length.

contentBlocks.value: Check the other pair too: PQ = (3, 5) − (−2, 4) = (5, 1) = OR
Result: Both pairs of opposite sides are equal and parallel, so OPQR is a parallelogram

strategyBlocks.value: Read OR from the grid, subtract QR from R's coordinates to locate Q, apply Pythagoras for the magnitude, then show a pair of opposite sides are equal vectors.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (iii) OR = (5, 1)  (iv) Q = (3, 5)  (v) |QR| = √20 = 2√5 ≈ 4.47 units  (vi) OP = (−2, 4) and RQ = (−2, 4), so OP = RQ; also PQ = (5, 1) = OR. Both pairs of opposite sides are equal in length and parallel, therefore OPQR is a parallelogram.

whyThisWorks.value: A position vector is just the point's coordinates written as a column, so reading the grid gives OR directly. The vector QR is the displacement from Q to R, so undoing it from R lands you back on Q. Two sides of a quadrilateral being represented by identical column vectors means they have the same direction and the same length — and that is precisely the definition of a parallelogram.

examTip.value: When testing a parallelogram with vectors, always take the two opposite sides in the same rotational direction round the shape, or the signs will fight you.
